---
title: Relying Parties
---

Reference tables for identifying and grouping the services that use CanadaLogin,
in the `rp` schema. They hold no measurements. They exist to give the analytics
tables a shared service identifier, so that IBM Verify sign-in counts and Google
Analytics funnel steps can be reported against the same list of services.

`service` holds one row per relying party, with its names, operator, and launch
date. `alias` maps each of the many strings the source systems use for a service
back to that service's `rp_id`.

Both tables come from one hand-maintained
[Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11czXAX6mTxZbbcH_XbFmI-TSoSTc2M5FXUp9teGw1D0/edit?gid=0#gid=0),
read every weekday by the `rp-sync` Lambda in
[`cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline).
That pipeline owns the table structure. Do not change it from this side.

### Joining through the lookup

Resolve a source-system name to a relying party by joining on `alias`, then join
`rp_id` to `service` for the attributes:

```sql
SELECT s.service_name_en,
       sum(a.successful_logins) AS successful_logins
FROM ibm_verify.app_login_counts a
JOIN rp.alias al ON a.application_name = al.alias
JOIN rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
WHERE a.from_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-07-01' AND DATE '2026-07-31'
GROUP BY s.service_name_en
```

Aggregate after the join, never before. Several IBM Verify application names can
map to one service, so a pre-aggregated count keyed on `application_name` will
split a service across its environments.

### Data quality

Because the source is a hand-maintained spreadsheet, a few caveats apply to both
tables:

- **The list is not a complete inventory.** Services are added when they appear
  in IBM Verify or analytics data, so a live service with no traffic yet will be missing.
- **New names need a manual edit.** An application name that appears in IBM
  Verify before someone adds it to the sheet will not resolve, and an inner join
  will drop its rows without complaint. Left join and check for nulls when you
  care about coverage.
- **Free-text columns are unvalidated.** `service_name_en`, `service_name_fr`,
  and `operator` are typed by hand, so expect occasional drift in spelling and
  spacing. Group by `gc_orgid` rather than `operator`.
- **Neither table keeps history.** Each refresh overwrites the previous one, so
  a service renamed in the sheet is renamed retroactively for every report.
